Today, Apple held an opening ceremony for its Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston, Texas. Details are as follows.

Apple to provide training for business leaders at its newly launched Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston

Apple today opened its brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses for small and medium-sized enterprises, allowing them to experience firsthand the most advanced equipment, interactive labs, and various tools to accelerate innovation. The Advanced Manufacturing Center is located at the same site as Apple's Houston facility, which produces and ships Apple's cutting-edge AI servers, and will begin producing Mac mini later this year... Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars in this Houston facility. We have built the factory, started production, and shipped the first batch of advanced AI servers from here. Today we are delighted to open this brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which will be a place where business leaders, workers, and students can learn the same innovative processes we use to manufacture Apple's most groundbreaking products. We also look forward to starting production of Mac mini later this year. We believe in the strength of American workers and American creativity, and we are moving forward at a remarkable pace, because what we want to create is not just outstanding products—what we want to build is the future of American manufacturing."

Tim Cook announced his Houston trip via social media and traveled there in person to attend the opening ceremony. Guests attending the ceremony included U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Congressman Christian Menefee, and Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis.

The Advanced Manufacturing Center covers an area of 20,000 square feet, where Apple's experts will "share knowledge directly with participating businesses and entrepreneurs within the center, helping to accelerate the development of smart manufacturing in the United States."

The first batch of business leaders have arrived today to attend the opening training session. The day's topics revolved around smart manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
